# Use AI thoughtfully in research

[← Main guide](../README.md) · [Browse resources](resources.md)

AI literacy has several entry points. Practical LLM use can begin early; training biological models and building tool-using agents require deeper foundations. Keep the scientific question and evidence visible at every stage.

## Along this path

- [Machine learning and biological models](#model-foundations)
- [Working with LLMs for science](#llms)
- [Agentic AI and scientific tools](#agents)
- [Evaluate and document AI-assisted work](#ai-evaluation)

<a id="model-foundations"></a>

## Machine learning and biological models

**Level:** Intermediate

Learn what a model represents, optimizes, and can reasonably generalize to.

**Before you begin:** Basic Python, statistics, and introductory linear algebra.

### What to understand

- Training, validation, test sets, leakage, baselines, and distribution shift.
- Embeddings and transformers; variational autoencoders and latent variables.
- Diffusion and conditional generation, with links to molecular design.
- Using a pretrained model versus fine-tuning or training a new one.

### What you’ll be able to do

Describe a model's objective, input representation, baseline, and evaluation task.

### Try this

Read one scvi-tools model guide and one protein-design model description. Compare their inputs, objectives, outputs, and evidence of usefulness.

### Keep in mind

A benchmark score only speaks to its evaluation setup. Ask how data were split and whether the test resembles the intended scientific application.

### A few good resources

- [Dive into Deep Learning](https://d2l.ai/) — Book · Intermediate · Free online · English. Build conceptual and practical foundations in deep learning; select chapters relevant to the model you are studying.
  - Prerequisites: Python, probability, linear algebra, and basic calculus for deeper chapters.

- [Google Machine Learning Crash Course](https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course) — Course · Intermediate · Free · English. An applied introduction to model fitting, generalization, data handling, and evaluation.
  - Prerequisites: Python and introductory algebra/statistics; check module guidance.

- [scvi-tools tutorials and model guides](https://docs.scvi-tools.org/en/stable/) — Documentation · Advanced · Free; compute may cost · English. Choose probabilistic models by task and modality, and read their assumptions alongside the worked tutorials.
  - Prerequisites: Python, single-cell analysis, and statistics.

- [RFdiffusion](https://github.com/RosettaCommons/RFdiffusion) — Tool · Advanced · Code available; GPU compute may cost · English. Explore diffusion-based protein backbone generation and conditional design through the authors' code and examples.
  - Prerequisites: Protein design, structure assessment, and command-line experience.

<a id="llms"></a>

## Working with LLMs for science

**Level:** Beginner

Use an LLM for bounded tasks with explicit context and inspectable outputs.

**Before you begin:** A clear task and the ability to assess the result or consult a qualified reviewer.

### What to understand

- Provide the question, source material, constraints, and desired output format.
- Ground literature summaries in supplied papers and check claims against the original text.
- For code assistance, provide schemas and small examples, inspect changes, and run meaningful checks.
- Record the model, date, inputs, important instructions, and human verification.

### What you’ll be able to do

Create a useful research aid with a record of its sources and checks.

### Try this

Give an LLM a paper's methods section and ask for a table of reported parameters with supporting quotations and locations. Mark absent information as not reported, then verify every row yourself.

### Keep in mind

Fluent output can contain incorrect claims, citations, or code. Use suitable public or authorized data and check the service's data-handling terms before supplying unpublished or sensitive material.

### A few good resources

- [Ten simple rules for using large language models in science](https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011767) — Paper · Beginner · Open access · English. A science-specific starting point for transparent, critical LLM use, with discussion of verification and appropriate applications.
  - Prerequisites: A scientific task you want to support with an LLM.

- [Developing Software with Generative AI](https://carpentries-incubator.github.io/software-development-with-genai/) — Tutorial · Intermediate · Free · English. Practice AI-assisted software development through a research-computing lesson. The material is under development; check its current status and verify generated code.
  - Prerequisites: Some programming experience; this is an evolving Carpentries Incubator lesson.

- [Hugging Face LLM course](https://huggingface.co/learn/llm-course/chapter1/1) — Course · Intermediate · Free; optional compute may cost · English. Understand language models and their practical ecosystem; pair technical learning with source verification and task-level checks.
  - Prerequisites: Python and introductory machine learning for implementation chapters.

<a id="agents"></a>

## Agentic AI and scientific tools

**Level:** Advanced

Connect a model to tools while keeping execution and evaluation observable.

**Before you begin:** Programming, APIs, practical LLM use, and a reproducible baseline task.

### What to understand

- Tool calling, structured inputs and outputs, retrieval, state, and execution traces.
- Bounded tool permissions, explicit stopping conditions, and human review where needed.
- Task-level evaluation, failure cases, tool-result verification, and cost tracking.

### What you’ll be able to do

Specify and evaluate a small agent against a simpler scripted baseline.

### Try this

Build a read-only assistant over a few public tutorials. Require source locations for answers and test it on a fixed set of answerable and unanswerable questions.

### Keep in mind

Start with a narrow task and inspect the trace. Greater autonomy is not itself evidence of better scientific results.

### A few good resources

- [Hugging Face Agents Course](https://huggingface.co/learn/agents-course/unit0/introduction) — Course · Advanced · Course free; external services may cost · English. An introduction to agent concepts, tools, and implementation. Evaluate any example on a bounded scientific task before expanding it.
  - Prerequisites: Python, APIs, and basic LLM familiarity.

- [Developing Software with Generative AI](https://carpentries-incubator.github.io/software-development-with-genai/) — Tutorial · Intermediate · Free · English. Practice AI-assisted software development through a research-computing lesson. The material is under development; check its current status and verify generated code.
  - Prerequisites: Some programming experience; this is an evolving Carpentries Incubator lesson.

<a id="ai-evaluation"></a>

## Evaluate and document AI-assisted work

**Level:** Intermediate

Make it clear which results come from evidence, computation, and model suggestions.

**Before you begin:** Practical LLM experience or an introductory machine-learning project.

### What to understand

- Reference examples, baselines, held-out tasks, and explicit success criteria.
- Citation verification, numerical checks, reproducible tool outputs, and failure analysis.
- Versioned prompts or instructions, model settings, tool versions, and limitations.

### What you’ll be able to do

Write a short evaluation report with successes, failures, and reproducibility details.

### Try this

Compare an LLM-assisted solution with a manual or scripted baseline on five fixed tasks. Report factual accuracy and completion, not just writing quality.

### Keep in mind

The model's own confidence is not an independent check. Verify important claims and calculations against external evidence or deterministic computation.

### A few good resources

- [Ten simple rules for using large language models in science](https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1011767) — Paper · Beginner · Open access · English. A science-specific starting point for transparent, critical LLM use, with discussion of verification and appropriate applications.
  - Prerequisites: A scientific task you want to support with an LLM.

- [Developing Software with Generative AI](https://carpentries-incubator.github.io/software-development-with-genai/) — Tutorial · Intermediate · Free · English. Practice AI-assisted software development through a research-computing lesson. The material is under development; check its current status and verify generated code.
  - Prerequisites: Some programming experience; this is an evolving Carpentries Incubator lesson.

- [Hugging Face Agents Course](https://huggingface.co/learn/agents-course/unit0/introduction) — Course · Advanced · Course free; external services may cost · English. An introduction to agent concepts, tools, and implementation. Evaluate any example on a bounded scientific task before expanding it.
  - Prerequisites: Python, APIs, and basic LLM familiarity.

- [Quarto: getting started](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) — Tutorial · Beginner · Free · English. Combine analysis, narrative, and outputs in a reproducible report rather than copying results into an unrelated document.
  - Prerequisites: Basic R or Python for executable examples.
